# Simple English for OpenCode

Rewrite the given text into simple English.

Rule: every word must earn its place. If you can cut it without losing meaning, cut it.

Write for a tired reader who will read each sentence once. Prefer short sentences, plain words, active voice, and one meaning per word. AI padding dies as a side effect.

Use this for marketing copy, technical docs, blog posts, specs, and AI-generated text. It is not a full ASD-STE100 compliance tool. It takes the useful parts of Simplified Technical English (short sentences, active voice, fixed vocabulary, self-check) and applies them to broader prose, including marketing and blogs.

## Your task

1. Classify each passage as procedural (instructions) or descriptive (explanations). Do not mix the two in one paragraph.
2. Pick vocabulary before drafting: one verb for check/verify/confirm/validate; one noun for config/settings/options. Keep those choices for the whole piece.
3. Rewrite under the rules below. Do not explain while drafting. Rewrite first.
4. Run the self-check. Mandatory.
5. Deliver in the fixed output format. No other sections unless the user asked for Check mode.

Never invent facts, metrics, product claims, or citations the source did not contain. If a claim is empty ("enterprise-grade", "blazingly fast"), cut it or replace it with a concrete fact already in the source. If none exists, cut it.

## Modes

| Mode              | Trigger                                   | Output                                                          |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rewrite (default) | rewrite, simplify, de-slop, plain English | Fixed format below                                              |
| Check             | check, audit, review only, just findings  | Findings table only. No full rewrite.                           |
| Shorter           | make it shorter, cut hard                 | Same as Rewrite, with hard cuts (aim for about 30% fewer words) |

Genre hints (optional): `marketing`, `docs`, `blog`, `spec`. Apply the matching notes in `references/genres.md`. Default genre = match the source.

## Rules

### Sentences

| Passage type | Limit    | Shape                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedural   | 20 words | Imperative. One instruction per sentence. Condition before command: "If the build fails, read the log." |
| Descriptive  | 25 words | Simple present / past / future. One topic per paragraph. Max six sentences per paragraph.               |

- No semicolons. Split into two sentences.
- No contractions in technical docs/specs (`you'll` → `you will`). Marketing and blogs may keep contractions if they fit the voice.
- Keep articles and "that" when they prevent misreading: "Make sure that the file exists."
- Prefer two short sentences over one clever long one.

### Verbs and voice

- Active voice. Passive is allowed only when the actor is unknown, or the genre is a formal spec and the object matters more than the actor.
- Prefer simple tenses. Avoid present perfect padding ("has been completed" → "completed" / "is complete").
- Do not hang meaning on `-ing` clauses after a comma (", making it easy" → new sentence with a real subject).
- Approved modals for requirements and facts: can, will, must. Treat should / would / may / might / could as soft AI hedges. Replace with must/can, state the fact, or delete.
- Prefer verbs over nouns: "decide", not "make a decision"; "compress the file", not "perform compression of the file".

### Words

- One word, one meaning, for the whole document. No synonym rotation.
- Noun chains of three words or fewer. Break longer chains with prepositions: "the timeout value for the connection pool".
- Delete words that carry no fact. Replace AI/corporate filler using `references/substitutions.md`.
- Prefer concrete nouns and strong verbs over adjectives and adverbs. "Ran quickly" → "sprinted". "Very large" → give the number or cut "very".
- American English spelling unless the source is clearly British and the user wants to keep it.

### Untouchables

Leave these exact (each counts as one word toward sentence limits when backticked or quoted):

- Code, identifiers, CLI commands, flags, file paths
- Quoted errors and log lines
- Product names, API routes, config keys
- Numbers with units already in the source

### AI-slop kills (always)

Delete or rewrite every instance of:

| Pattern                                                                               | Fix                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Enthusiasm padding ("Great question!", "Absolutely!")                                 | Delete                                   |
| Filler transitions ("Let's dive in", "In this article we will")                       | Delete or state the point                |
| Fake structure ("In conclusion…") that restates                                       | Delete                                   |
| Empty intensifiers (truly, incredibly, remarkably, seamlessly, robust, comprehensive) | Delete or give a measure from the source |
| Thesaurus triples ("efficient, effective, and streamlined")                           | Keep one word                            |
| Hollow claims with no proof                                                           | Cut, or keep only sourced facts          |
| Emoji seasoning that adds no meaning                                                  | Delete                                   |

## Fixed output format

Use this exact structure. Do not add a preamble. Do not wrap the whole reply in a code fence.

### Rewrite mode / Shorter mode

```markdown
## Simple English

[Full rewritten text. Preserve useful structure: headings, lists, links.
Keep untouchables exact.]

## Cuts

| Before                    | After            | Why          |
| ------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------ |
| quoted phrase or sentence | rewrite or (cut) | short reason |

List the 3–8 highest-value cuts only. Skip trivia.

## Stats

|                      | Before | After |
| -------------------- | ------ | ----- |
| Words                | N      | N     |
| Sentences            | N      | N     |
| Avg words / sentence | N      | N     |
| Passive voice        | N      | N     |
```

Approximate word counts are fine. Be consistent within the reply.

### Check mode

```markdown
## Findings

| #   | Issue                                                        | Quote | Fix     |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----- | ------- |
| 1   | long sentence / passive / filler / synonym / hedge / AI slop | "…"   | rewrite |

## Stats

| Words | Sentences | Avg | Passive | Filler hits |
| ----- | --------- | --- | ------- | ----------- |
| N     | N         | N   | N       | N           |
```

No full rewrite in Check mode unless the user asks for one after.

## Self-check (mandatory)

Before you deliver, run these four passes. Fix what you find.

1. Count words in your three longest sentences. Over 20 (procedural) or 25 (descriptive) → split.
2. Search for: contractions (docs/specs), `has been` / `have been`, `should` / `would` / `might`, `, making` / `, allowing` / `, enabling`, semicolons, `utilize` / `leverage` / `robust` / `seamless`.
3. Every `if` / `when` in a procedure stands at the start of its sentence, before the command.
4. Synonym scan: check/verify/confirm/validate and config/settings/options. One term each.

For a longer audit, use `references/checklist.md`.

## Example

**Input:**

> The decision was made by the committee to utilize a more robust framework that would facilitate better outcomes for all stakeholders involved in the process.

**Output:**

```markdown
## Simple English

The committee chose a stronger framework.

## Cuts

| Before                                                  | After               | Why                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------- |
| The decision was made by the committee                  | The committee chose | active voice          |
| utilize                                                 | chose / use         | plain verb            |
| robust framework that would facilitate better outcomes… | stronger framework  | empty claim + padding |

## Stats

|                      | Before | After |
| -------------------- | ------ | ----- |
| Words                | 26     | 6     |
| Sentences            | 1      | 1     |
| Avg words / sentence | 26     | 6     |
| Passive voice        | 1      | 0     |
```

## Remember

Short sentences. Plain words. Active voice. One meaning per word. Cut what does not earn its place. Deliver the rewrite first.

# Simple English for OpenCode

An OpenCode skill that rewrites verbose, AI-sounding prose into plain English.

Use it on marketing copy, docs, blog posts, specs, and AI-generated text. It keeps the discipline from [SimpleEnglish](https://github.com/AminBlg/SimpleEnglish) (short sentences, active voice, fixed vocabulary), but it is not a full ASD-STE100 compliance tool. It's a practical rewrite skill for real writing work.

## What it does

- Rewrites into short, plain, active sentences (max 20 words for steps, 25 for explanations)
- Cuts AI padding: filler transitions, empty intensifiers, fake structure, synonym rotation
- Locks vocabulary (one word, one meaning)
- Leaves code, identifiers, and quoted errors alone
- Returns the same three blocks every time: rewrite, cuts, and before/after stats

## Why use it

Most writing tools stop at flagging problems. This one rewrites the text into a cleaner version you can use.

It is built for cases where the draft is technically fine but still feels bloated, vague, or LLM-written:

- landing pages that sound like brochure copy
- docs that bury the point
- blog intros that take too long to start
- specs full of soft language and filler
- AI drafts that need a human, direct voice

## Modes

| Mode              | Say                                               | Result                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Rewrite (default) | "rewrite", "simplify", "de-slop", "plain English" | Simple English + Cuts + Stats                  |
| Check             | "check", "audit", "review only"                   | Findings table + Stats                         |
| Shorter           | "make it shorter"                                 | Same as rewrite, aim for about 30% fewer words |

Optional genre hint: `marketing`, `docs`, `blog`, or `spec`.

## Install

OpenCode loads skills from project and global directories.

### Global (recommended)

Clone the repo, then symlink the skill into your OpenCode skills directory:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/TMFNK/Simple-English-OpenCode.git
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/skills
ln -s "$(pwd)/Simple-English-OpenCode/skills/simple-english-opencode" \
  ~/.config/opencode/skills/simple-english-opencode
```

If you already have the repo elsewhere on disk, point the symlink at that path instead.

Or copy the skill directory:

```bash
cp -r skills/simple-english-opencode ~/.config/opencode/skills/simple-english-opencode
```

### Project-local

```bash
mkdir -p .opencode/skills
ln -s /path/to/simple-english-opencode/skills/simple-english-opencode \
  .opencode/skills/simple-english-opencode
```

OpenCode also picks up `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`. Start a new session after install. The agent should list `simple-english-opencode` in the `skill` tool.

Ask for a rewrite the way you normally would:

- "Rewrite this landing page in simple English."
- "De-slop this README."
- "Check this spec for filler and passive voice."
- "Make this blog intro shorter."
- "Marketing pass on this paragraph."

Optional genre hints:

# Real-world before/after: Shopify Enterprise page

Source page: [Shopify Enterprise](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise)  
Captured: 2026-08-04  
Use: demo of how `simple-english-opencode` rewrites high-traffic marketing copy.

## Before (excerpt from source page)

> Shopify is the enterprise commerce operating system for immediate success and future resilience. Designed to optimize resources and maximize returns, it keeps you ahead of shifting customer needs, amplifies your development team's impact, and helps you outsmart competitors instead of outspending them.
>
> Innovate and launch at lightning speed, on the only platform that’s consistently first-to-market with new capabilities.
>
> Increase top-line revenue with the best-converting checkout on the planet, and reach more customers on more channels.

## After (simple English rewrite)

```markdown
## Simple English

Shopify is a commerce platform for enterprise teams.
It helps teams launch faster and run global storefronts.

The platform is built to improve speed, uptime, and developer output.
Shopify says teams can ship new features faster and lower ownership costs.

Its checkout is positioned as a strong conversion driver.
The platform also supports selling across more channels.

## Cuts

| Before | After | Why |
|--------|-------|-----|
| immediate success and future resilience | launch faster and run global storefronts | vague phrase replaced with concrete outcome |
| optimize resources and maximize returns | lower ownership costs | shorter and more specific |
| outsmart competitors instead of outspending them | ship new features faster | marketing spin trimmed |
| at lightning speed, on the only platform... | ship new features faster | hype and exclusivity claim removed |
| best-converting checkout on the planet | strong conversion driver | unsupported superlative softened |

## Stats

| | Before | After |
|--|--------|-------|
| Words | 85 | 50 |
| Sentences | 3 | 6 |
| Avg words / sentence | 28 | 8 |
| Passive voice | 0 | 0 |
```

## Notes

- This keeps claims that are directionally useful while removing hype words and broad superlatives.
- Numbers are approximate and shown to mirror the skill's output contract.

# Verification checklist

Run after drafting. Ordered from mechanical to judgment.

## Mechanical (searchable)

Every hit outside code and quoted text is a problem.

| Search                                                                 | Problem               | Fix                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `utilize`, `leverage`, `facilitate`                                    | corporate filler      | use / help / enable                     |
| `simply`, `just`, `easily`, `seamlessly`, `effortlessly`               | empty intensifier     | delete                                  |
| `robust`, `powerful`, `comprehensive`, `performant`, `seamless`        | empty adjective       | delete or give a number from the source |
| `in order to`, `due to the fact that`, `prior to`, `in the event that` | padded phrase         | to / because / before / if              |
| `has been`, `have been`, `had been`                                    | perfect-tense padding | simple past or simple present           |
| `is being`, `are being`, `was being`                                   | progressive passive   | active, simple tense                    |
| `, making`, `, allowing`, `, enabling`, `, ensuring`                   | dangling -ing clause  | new sentence with a subject             |
| `should`, `would`, `may`, `might`, `could`                             | soft hedge            | must / can / fact / delete              |
| `;`                                                                    | semicolon             | two sentences                           |
| `Let's dive`, `In this article`, `In conclusion`, `Great question`     | AI scaffolding        | delete                                  |
| mid-sentence `if` / `when` in procedures                               | trailing condition    | move condition to the start             |

## Countable

1. Sentence length: procedural max 20 words; descriptive max 25.
2. Paragraph size: max 6 sentences; one topic.
3. Noun chains: max 3 words; break longer ones with of/on/in/for.
4. Instructions per sentence: one (unless simultaneous).

## Judgment

5. Classification: procedural vs descriptive cleanly split.
6. Voice: passive only when actor unknown or formal-spec object focus.
7. Vocabulary lock: one term for check/verify/confirm; one for config/settings.
8. Untouchables: code, paths, product names, quoted errors unchanged.
9. No invented facts: cuts only; never add metrics the source lacked.
10. Output shape: Rewrite/Check format matched exactly.

# Genre notes

Apply on top of the core rules when the user names a genre, or when the source clearly matches one. Keep these short. Do not invent new output sections.

## Marketing / product copy

Goal: clear value, not brochure fog.

- Keep persuasion. Cut empty claims. Every claim needs a number, name, or concrete detail already in the source. Otherwise cut it.
- One primary benefit early. One clear CTA. Multiple CTAs dilute.
- Kill: seamless, end-to-end, best-in-class, AI-powered (say what the AI does), empower, unlock, supercharge, game-changer.
- Contractions are fine if they match the brand voice.
- Sentence limits still apply. Punchy is not the same as vague.

## Technical docs / READMEs / runbooks

Goal: a tired operator cannot misread the step.

- Procedural sections: imperative, max 20 words, condition before command.
- Descriptive sections: max 25 words, no imperative.
- No contractions. Keep "that".
- Warnings: command or condition first, risk second.
- Untouchables stay exact.

## Blog (technical or general)

Goal: readable narrative without AI scaffolding.

- Hook in the first 50 words: problem or surprising fact, not a definition.
- Prefer prose over bullet spam when two or three sentences read better.
- Explain why before a code block. Show a short example when a claim needs proof.
- Delete "In this post we will…" and "In conclusion…".
- Contractions are fine.

## Specs / RFCs / design docs

Goal: precise and testable.

- Prefer must/can over should/may.
- Ambiguous words (fast, lightweight, scalable): demand numbers from the source or flag them in Cuts/Findings.
- Expand acronyms on first use.
- Passive voice is fine when the system is the actor and the object matters: "The request is validated against the schema."
- Structure beats style. Use lists and tables over narrative when requirements must be checked one by one.

## AI-generated text (any genre)

Always on when the source reads like a model default.

- Run the AI-slop kills in `SKILL.md` first.
- Collapse synonym rotation.
- Remove positivity without evidence.
- Prefer stance and specifics over both-sides hedging.

# Substitutions

If a word carries no fact, delete it. Do not replace fluff with different fluff.

## Corporate / AI filler

| Cut or replace                    | Prefer                                 |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| utilize, leverage                 | use                                    |
| facilitate                        | help, make possible                    |
| implement (vague)                 | do, start, build, run                  |
| prioritize                        | focus on                               |
| optimize (vague)                  | improve (say what)                     |
| functionality                     | function, feature                      |
| enables you to, allows you to     | you can                                |
| is designed to, aims to, seeks to | (delete; say what it does)             |
| in order to                       | to                                     |
| prior to                          | before                                 |
| in the event that                 | if                                     |
| due to the fact that              | because                                |
| with regard to, when it comes to  | for, about                             |
| a large number of                 | many / N                               |
| plethora, myriad                  | many                                   |
| as well as                        | and                                    |
| and/or                            | pick one, or "X, or Y, or both"        |
| e.g. / i.e. / etc.                | for example / that is / name the items |

## Empty intensifiers (usually delete)

simply, just, easily, seamlessly, effortlessly, truly, incredibly, remarkably, significantly (unless a number follows), very, really, extremely, quite, rather, basically, actually, literally

## Empty adjectives (delete or make concrete)

robust, powerful, comprehensive, performant, seamless, innovative, disruptive, cutting-edge, next-generation, best-in-class, enterprise-grade, world-class, holistic, impactful, scalable (unless you state the scale)

## Weak constructions

| Before                         | After                                   |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| make a decision                | decide                                  |
| perform an analysis of         | analyze                                 |
| provide assistance             | help                                    |
| take into consideration        | consider                                |
| it is important to note that   | (delete; state the fact)                |
| it should be noted that        | (delete or name who notes it)           |
| some people say / studies show | cite or delete                          |
| circle back                    | follow up                               |
| deep dive / delve into         | read, examine, review                   |
| bandwidth (for time)           | time, capacity                          |
| learnings                      | lessons                                 |
| deliverables                   | work, results                           |
| stakeholders                   | people / team / customers (be specific) |

## Modal ladder

| Soft                              | Prefer                            |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| should (requirement)              | must                              |
| should (nice-to-have)             | delete, or state why it is better |
| may / might / could (possibility) | can                               |
| would (hypothetical)              | "If X happens, Y happens."        |

## Consistency locks

Pick one per document and keep it:

| Concept            | Pick one                                           |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| checking           | check or verify or confirm or make sure            |
| configuration      | config or configuration or settings                |
| starting a process | run or start or execute                            |
| removing           | delete or remove (one meaning each if both needed) |
| problems           | error (defects) / failure (failed runs)            |
| showing            | show or display                                    |
